cards.text: John's writing to believers, and he calls them children. He opens BIG: it is the last hour, and they've heard that the antichrist is coming. Friend, that is NOT a snooze-button announcement.

cards.question: The believers have heard the antichrist is coming. What does John say has already happened?

cards.text: John says that's how they know it's the last hour. Then he says something about these antichrists that hits a little too close to home.

cards.question: True or false: John says these antichrists went out from among the believers.

cards.text: But here's the twist, friend: John says they did not belong to the believers.

cards.question: John says that if those people had really belonged to the believers, they would have ___ with them.

cards.text: Their leaving made it clear none of them belonged, like that little "left the group chat" notice that says EVERYTHING. Then John turns back to the believers, and this part is GOOD news.

cards.question: What does John say the believers have from the Holy One?
True or false: John says he's writing to the believers because they don't know the truth yet.

cards.text: John says no lie comes from the truth. Then he asks who the liar is, and friend, he does NOT leave you hanging on a cliffhanger.

cards.question: Who does John call the liar?

answers.text: Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ

cards.question: John says the antichrist is the one who denies the ___ and the ___.
True or false: John says a person can deny the Son and still have the Father.

cards.text: Whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well. Now John gives the believers their job, and it comes with a promise attached.

cards.question: What does John tell the believers to let remain in them?

answers.text: What they heard from the beginning
The words of the ones who left

cards.text: If that message remains in them, John says they'll remain in the Son and in the Father. Then he brings up a promise He Himself made, and unlike the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with, this one does NOT expire.

cards.question: John says the promise He Himself made to the believers is eternal ___.
True or false: John says he has written these things about those who are trying to deceive the believers.

cards.text: Last word, and John comes back to that anointing. It remains in them, they don't need anyone to teach them, and His true and genuine anointing teaches them about all things.

cards.question: With that anointing teaching them, what does John tell the believers to do?

answers.text: Remain in Him as they were taught
Go bring back the ones who left

findings.problem: The opening card says "John's writing to believers" but never says who John is, and gives no reference for him being the writer. 1 John never names its author in the BSB text, so introducing him as "John, one of Jesus' apostles" would rest on church tradition, not on a verse.
findings.question: For a letter whose author is not named in its text, like 1 John, how should Papa Dorin name and introduce the writer, and what reference, if any, should go with it?

findings.problem: The wrong answers "quarreled" and "traveled" don't fit a sentence about what people who truly belonged would have done with the believers. "Quarreled" in particular is not believable as a sign of belonging, so "remained" is the only reasonable pick.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Verse 20b, "and all of you know the truth," is never told or asked. Card 8 cites 1 John 2:20 but covers only the anointing. Card 9 then asks why John is writing without the baker ever hearing that the believers know the truth.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: No story card sets up this true or false question. Because 1 John 2:20's "all of you know the truth" was never told, the baker has nothing to reason from about why John is writing.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "He does NOT leave you hanging on a cliffhanger" is redundant and isn't a real laugh. It reads like filler, not like Papa Dorin's laugh-out-loud voice.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question types fall into a repeating rhythm. Multiple choice opens each cycle, followed by true or false and fill in the blank: MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, MC, FB, TF, MC, FB, TF, MC. Cards 11–13 and 15–18 repeat the same MC, FB, TF order.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
